item.description:
Improvements

  • **Claude Desktop web search through the gateway.** The Desktop's built-in web-search server now runs against LittleSwitch itself: searches execute on the configured provider (Firecrawl or Tavily), honor the results limit, appear in Logs, and need no credential in any configuration file.
  • **The gateway speaks https and plain http on one port.** Claude Desktop rides https — its managed web-search contract accepts nothing else — while Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode keep plain http with no client-side migration. The first inbound byte decides.
  • **The https identity is a private loopback authority.** Its signing key is created in memory, signs exactly one leaf, and is destroyed before issuance returns; the anchor macOS trusts can never vouch for anything new. One consent prompt on first connect, then silence — toggling the Claude switch never re-prompts. Renewal is automatic inside a 30-day margin of the 825-day validity.
  • The menu's usage block now shows the token direction — input, cached, output — in a two-row grid instead of one blended total.
  • Every published version of Claude's built-in web-search tool is bridged as a direct call, so a client that upgraded to `web_search_20260209` or later no longer loses whole conversations to an HTTP 400.

Fixes

  • A missing web-search provider key now answers 503 "Web search credential is missing" instead of a misleading provider failure, matching the earlier 401 diagnosis fix.
  • Idle TCP connections to the gateway no longer park a task forever; silent peers and oversized handshakes are closed at the decision bound.
  • Claude Desktop's profile only advertises the https origin once the trust anchor is actually installed, so a dismissed or failed consent prompt degrades to plain http instead of cutting the Desktop off entirely.

Improvements

  • Codex's model picker now shows readable model names — `z.ai/glm-4.6`, `ollama/qwen3.5:9b-mlx` — instead of opaque encoded identifiers, described by the product name alone.
  • z.ai providers: the OpenAI-compatible coding path is the base URL and the Anthropic path becomes an optional second surface, editable in the provider form ("Anthropic URL (optional)"). Messages and count-tokens ride the Anthropic URL when present; discovery and chat completions mount at the base URL.
  • The provider form leads with the connection test outcome rows.

Fixes

  • vLLM providers: streaming responses with `null` reasoning content or absent function-call fields no longer masquerade as stream failures.
  • The Responses wire resolves by automatic detection again; the z.ai base-URL heuristic is gone.

Improvements

  • Codex's model picker now shows readable model names — `z.ai/glm-4.6`, `ollama/qwen3.5:9b-mlx` — instead of opaque encoded identifiers, described by the product name alone.
  • z.ai providers: the OpenAI-compatible coding path is the base URL and the Anthropic path becomes an optional second surface, editable in the provider form ("Anthropic URL (optional)"). Messages and count-tokens ride the Anthropic URL when present; discovery and chat completions mount at the base URL.
  • The provider form leads with the connection test outcome rows.

Fixes

  • vLLM providers: streaming responses with `null` reasoning content or absent function-call fields no longer masquerade as stream failures.
  • The Responses wire resolves by automatic detection again; the z.ai base-URL heuristic is gone.

Fixes

  • When a provider's model discovery cannot reach the endpoint, the error now names the actual connection problem — "Read timeout", "Remote connection closed" — instead of an opaque `(AsyncHTTPClient.HTTPClientError error 1.)`, so script-authenticated providers show whether the endpoint, not the script, is the one failing.

Always-there brand marks

  • The menu's Claude Desktop and Codex rows now show LittleSwitch's own bundled brand marks instead of borrowing the installed applications' icons, so every row reads correctly from the very first launch — no matter which apps are installed.

Fixes

  • Provider save failures are now reported inside the editor sheet instead of a generic app alert.

Live model remaps — Claude Code & Claude Desktop

  • Remapping a route now applies immediately to running Claude apps: no relaunch, and open conversations follow along.
  • The served model catalog is invariant: route IDs and display names never move, so clients keep their model picker selections across remaps.
  • New Model indicator setting: choose how mapped routes are marked in the served model lists (⇌ equilibrium, ⇄ swap, ⇢ routed, ↦ maps-to, or plain).

Tabbed status menu

  • The menu is now organized into Overview, Claude, and Codex tabs.
  • The Claude tab maps the Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku routes in place with steppers and a single Apply action; the Codex tab sets the default Codex model.
  • Each tab shows its client's 30-day token history chart.
  • Steppers preview the chosen model immediately and reconcile when the apply lands.

Fixes

  • Codex refusals now explain which agents form was refused instead of surfacing a raw error code.
  • Compact token counts hold steady at display-rounding boundaries.
  • Menu tab content spacing is balanced top and bottom.
